EnvironmentalPhenomenon


The actual or forecast characteristics of an environmental phenomenon at a specific point in time (or during a specific time interval) that may have both a center and area/line location.

  • EnvironmentalPhenomenon
  • AtmosphericPhenomenon
  • CloudCondition
  • Cyclone
  • Earthquake
  • Fire
  • Flood
  • GeosphericPhenomenon
  • HydrosphericPhenomenon
  • Landslide
  • LightningStrike
  • MagneticStorm
  • SpacePhenomenon
  • Tornado
  • Tsunami
  • VolcanicAshCloud
  • Whirlpool
root anyOf EnvironmentalPhenomenon

EnvironmentalPhenomenon

Type: object

The actual or forecast characteristics of an environmental phenomenon at a specific point in time (or during a specific time interval) that may have both a center and area/line location.

 No Additional Properties

root anyOf EnvironmentalPhenomenon EnvironmentalPhenomenon.EnvironmentalInformation

EnvironmentalInformation

Type: object

Abstract class (with concrete child classes of Observation and Forecast) that groups phenomenon and/or environmental value sets.

 No Additional Properties

root anyOf EnvironmentalPhenomenon EnvironmentalPhenomenon.EnvironmentalInformation EnvironmentalInformation.created

created

Type: string

The timestamp of when the forecast was created

root anyOf EnvironmentalPhenomenon EnvironmentalPhenomenon.EnvironmentalInformation Ravens.cimObjectType

cimObjectType

Type: enum (of string)

Used in RAVENS Schema to identify the corresponding CIM Object Type of the JSON object.

Must be one of:

  • "EnvironmentalInformation"

root anyOf EnvironmentalPhenomenon EnvironmentalPhenomenon.EnvironmentalInformation IdentifiedObject.name

name

Type: string

The name is any free human readable and possibly non unique text naming the object.

root anyOf EnvironmentalPhenomenon EnvironmentalPhenomenon.EnvironmentalInformation IdentifiedObject.description

description

Type: string

The description is a free human readable text describing or naming the object. It may be non unique and may not correlate to a naming hierarchy.

root anyOf EnvironmentalPhenomenon EnvironmentalPhenomenon.EnvironmentalInformation IdentifiedObject.aliasName

aliasName

Type: string

The aliasName is free text human readable name of the object alternative to IdentifiedObject.name. It may be non unique and may not correlate to a naming hierarchy.
The attribute aliasName is retained because of backwards compatibility between CIM relases. It is however recommended to replace aliasName with the Name class as aliasName is planned for retirement at a future time.

root anyOf EnvironmentalPhenomenon EnvironmentalPhenomenon.EnvironmentalInformation IdentifiedObject.mRID

mRID

Type: string

Master resource identifier issued by a model authority. The mRID is unique within an exchange context. Global uniqueness is easily achieved by using a UUID, as specified in RFC 4122, for the mRID. The use of UUID is strongly recommended.
For CIMXML data files in RDF syntax conforming to IEC 61970-552, the mRID is mapped to rdf:ID or rdf:about attributes that identify CIM object elements.

root anyOf EnvironmentalPhenomenon EnvironmentalPhenomenon.EnvironmentalInformation Forecast.validFor

validFor

Type: object

The interval for which the forecast is valid. For example, a forecast issued now for tomorrow might be valid for the next 2 hours.

 No Additional Properties

root anyOf EnvironmentalPhenomenon EnvironmentalPhenomenon.EnvironmentalInformation Forecast.validFor end
Type: string Default: null

End date and time of this interval. The end date and time where the interval is defined up to, but excluded.

root anyOf EnvironmentalPhenomenon EnvironmentalPhenomenon.EnvironmentalInformation Forecast.validFor start
Type: string Default: null

Start date and time of this interval. The start date and time is included in the defined interval.

root anyOf EnvironmentalPhenomenon LightningStrike.negativePolarity

negativePolarity

Type: boolean

The polarity of the strike, with T meaning negative. About 90% of all lightning strokes are negative strokes, meaning that they were initiated by a large concentration of negative charge in the cloud-base; this tends to induce an area of positive charge on the ground.

root anyOf EnvironmentalPhenomenon Earthquake.intensity

intensity

Type: integer

The intensity of the earthquake as defined by the Modified Mercalli Intensity (MMI) scale. Possible values are 1-12, corresponding to I-XII.

root anyOf EnvironmentalPhenomenon MagneticStorm.changeDst

changeDst

Type: object or number

Change in the disturbance - storm time (Dst) index. The size of a geomagnetic storm is classified as:
- moderate ( -50 nT >minimum of Dst > -100 nT)
- intense (-100 nT > minimum Dst > -250 nT) or
- super-storm ( minimum of Dst < -250 nT).

 No Additional Properties

root anyOf EnvironmentalPhenomenon TropicalCycloneAustralia.category

category

Type: integer

Strength of tropical cyclone during the time interval, based on Australian Bureau of Meteorology Category System where:
1 - tropical cyclone, with typical gusts over flat land 90-125 km/h
2 - tropical cyclone, with typical gusts over flat land 125-164 km/h
3 - severe tropical cyclone, with typical gusts over flat land 165-224 km/h
4 - severe tropical cyclone, with typical gusts over flat land 225-279 km/h
5 - severe tropical cyclone, with typical gusts over flat land greater than 280 km/h.

root anyOf AtmosphericPhenomenon TropicalCycloneAustralia.category

category

Type: integer

Strength of tropical cyclone during the time interval, based on Australian Bureau of Meteorology Category System where:
1 - tropical cyclone, with typical gusts over flat land 90-125 km/h
2 - tropical cyclone, with typical gusts over flat land 125-164 km/h
3 - severe tropical cyclone, with typical gusts over flat land 165-224 km/h
4 - severe tropical cyclone, with typical gusts over flat land 225-279 km/h
5 - severe tropical cyclone, with typical gusts over flat land greater than 280 km/h.

root anyOf Cyclone TropicalCycloneAustralia.category

category

Type: integer

Strength of tropical cyclone during the time interval, based on Australian Bureau of Meteorology Category System where:
1 - tropical cyclone, with typical gusts over flat land 90-125 km/h
2 - tropical cyclone, with typical gusts over flat land 125-164 km/h
3 - severe tropical cyclone, with typical gusts over flat land 165-224 km/h
4 - severe tropical cyclone, with typical gusts over flat land 225-279 km/h
5 - severe tropical cyclone, with typical gusts over flat land greater than 280 km/h.

root anyOf Earthquake Earthquake.magnitude

magnitude

Type: number

The magnitude of the earthquake as defined on the Moment Magnitude (M<sub>w</sub>) scale, which measures the size of earthquakes in terms of the energy released. Must be greater than zero.

root anyOf Earthquake Earthquake.intensity

intensity

Type: integer

The intensity of the earthquake as defined by the Modified Mercalli Intensity (MMI) scale. Possible values are 1-12, corresponding to I-XII.

root anyOf GeosphericPhenomenon LightningStrike.negativePolarity

negativePolarity

Type: boolean

The polarity of the strike, with T meaning negative. About 90% of all lightning strokes are negative strokes, meaning that they were initiated by a large concentration of negative charge in the cloud-base; this tends to induce an area of positive charge on the ground.

root anyOf LightningStrike LightningStrike.negativePolarity

negativePolarity

Type: boolean

The polarity of the strike, with T meaning negative. About 90% of all lightning strokes are negative strokes, meaning that they were initiated by a large concentration of negative charge in the cloud-base; this tends to induce an area of positive charge on the ground.

root anyOf MagneticStorm

MagneticStorm

Type: object

A magnetic storm, a temporary disturbance of the earth's magnetic field, induced by radiation and streams of charged particles from the sun.

 No Additional Properties

EnvironmentalInformation

Type: object

Abstract class (with concrete child classes of Observation and Forecast) that groups phenomenon and/or environmental value sets.

Same definition as EnvironmentalPhenomenon.EnvironmentalInformation

root anyOf MagneticStorm MagneticStorm.changeDst

changeDst

Type: object or number

Change in the disturbance - storm time (Dst) index. The size of a geomagnetic storm is classified as:
- moderate ( -50 nT >minimum of Dst > -100 nT)
- intense (-100 nT > minimum Dst > -250 nT) or
- super-storm ( minimum of Dst < -250 nT).

 No Additional Properties
